title: A 12-Year-Old vs a Shinobi: The Fight Hanzo Couldn't Win

cuts.voiceover_text: First match of the Hunter Exam final: Hanzo versus Gon. A small boy in green steps into the arena against a tall shinobi in dark garb. The mismatch is obvious.
Gon confirms the one rule that will define everything. You only win when your opponent surrenders. Knocking them out doesn't count.

The match starts. Gon takes off, quick on his feet. Hanzo just smiles and vanishes. In a flash of white he reappears behind him and drives Gon into the floor. Hanzo is faster and stronger in every way.
Hanzo stands over the bruised boy and tells him he doesn't stand a chance. Just give up and spare yourself the trouble. Gon lies on the ground, silent, refusing.

Three hours later, Gon still hasn't said the word. Hanzo pins his left arm to the ground and tells him to surrender or lose it. Gon whispers, try to stop me. Hanzo snaps the arm. It bends at an ugly angle across the stone floor.
Hanzo escalates. He tells Gon he'll cut off his legs, permanently, if he doesn't surrender. Gon, broken arm and all, just looks up and calmly refuses.

Finally Gon tells him why. His father is a Hunter, and he wants to become one to find him. If he surrenders here, he feels like he never will. So he won't give up. Hanzo, sweating and shaking, lifts his blade to the bloodied boy's forehead.
Surrender, Hanzo says, or you will die. Gon doesn't flinch. And then, for the first time all match, it's Hanzo who breaks. He lowers the blade and tells him, fine. You win. I give up.
But Gon refuses the win. He says he doesn't want to advance like this, that they have to find a way Hanzo can actually beat him. Hanzo stares in disbelief.

So Hanzo does the only thing left. One clean chop to the neck, and Gon drops unconscious. Hanzo concedes the match. Gon wins his first fight in the Hunter Exam, without ever saying the word surrender.
